instructions: Put the rice and 2 1/4 cups of water in a pot over high heat. Bring it to a boil, then cover, turn the heat to low and cook for 15 minutes. Take it off the heat and leave the lid on.
Fill a large pot with about 8 cups of water, enough to cover the thighs by 1 inch. Add 1 whole scallion and 5 slices of ginger and bring it to a boil over high heat.
Meanwhile, finely mince the white and light green parts of the other 5 scallions and 1/4 cup of the ginger. Transfer them to a heatproof bowl with 1/2 tsp of the salt.
Lower the thighs into the boiling water. When it comes back to a boil, turn the heat to the lowest setting and cover.

Poach for 20 to 25 minutes, with the water barely moving. You're cooking the chicken to 175°F in the thickest part, so if you have a thermometer, check it there. No thermometer? Poke the thickest part with a chopstick: the juices should run clear and there should be no pink at the bone.
While it poaches, fill a large bowl with cold water and a few big handfuls of ice.
Heat the oil in a small pot over high heat for about 2 minutes, until it shimmers. Stand back a little. Pour it over the scallion and ginger in the bowl. It will sizzle. Stir it.
Taste the sauce. If it's flat, add the last 1/2 tsp salt.
Transfer the thighs into the ice bath and leave them for 5 minutes, turning them once.
Cut the meat off the bones and slice it, skin on, into 1/2-inch pieces.
Serve the chicken with the ginger scallion oil spooned over and the rice.
method_notes: Lead is The Woks of Life (4.83 from 57), a whole chicken poached gently, chilled in an ice bath and served with a ginger scallion oil. Made With Lau and Whattocooktoday agree on the poach, ice bath and the oil poured hot over minced aromatics; Whattocooktoday uses drumsticks and a 40 minute poach. A whole bird takes about 70 minutes, which breaks the 45 minute target, so this uses bone-in thighs, poached about 20 to 25 minutes, and a larger batch of the oil. The soy sauce is left out to keep it gluten-free.
